title: Showing Your Opinion
text:
When people write opinion articles, they often use phrases that signal their stance. Words such as 'clearly' or 'surely' suggest the writer is confident, while 'perhaps' or 'it seems' show more caution. Choosing the right phrase helps the reader understand how strongly the author believes something.

However, a writer who uses too many strong phrases may seem unfair or aggressive. Readers often trust a balanced voice more, especially when the topic is controversial. For this reason, many editors advise writers to support their claims with evidence rather than rely only on confident language.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do words such as 'clearly' or 'surely' suggest?
options: That the writer is asking a question

questions.text: According to paragraph two, how might a writer who uses too many strong phrases be seen?
What can be inferred about readers of controversial topics?
options: They prefer writers who sound balanced
They only trust writers who use strong phrases
They prefer articles with no evidence

questions.text: What does the author suggest about the value of evidence in opinion writing?
options: Evidence makes an argument more convincing than confident language alone
Evidence is unnecessary if the writer is confident
Evidence only matters in scientific writing

vocabulary.definition: a person's opinion or position on a topic
careful to avoid risks or mistakes
fair, showing more than one side of an issue

paragraph_translations: Kiedy ludzie piszą artykuły opinii, często używają zwrotów, które sygnalizują ich stanowisko. Słowa takie jak 'clearly' czy 'surely' sugerują, że autor jest pewny siebie, a 'perhaps' lub 'it seems' pokazują większą ostrożność. Wybór odpowiedniego zwrotu pomaga czytelnikowi zrozumieć, jak mocno autor w coś wierzy.

Jednak autor, który używa zbyt wielu mocnych zwrotów, może wydawać się niesprawiedliwy lub agresywny. Czytelnicy często bardziej ufają wyważonemu głosowi, zwłaszcza gdy temat jest kontrowersyjny. Z tego powodu wielu redaktorów radzi autorom popierać swoje twierdzenia dowodami, a nie polegać wyłącznie na pewnym tonie.
